identity.title: Addressing divergent representations from causal interventions on neural networks

problem.claim: The paper asks whether causal interventions on neural representations create out-of-distribution states and compromise explanation faithfulness to the model’s natural behavior.

contributions.claim: Shows that common causal intervention techniques often shift internal representations away from the target model’s natural distribution.
Analyzes harmless divergences in a layer’s behavioral null-space and pernicious divergences that activate hidden pathways and produce dormant behavioral changes.
Applies and modifies the Counterfactual Latent loss to keep intervention-generated representations closer to the natural distribution while retaining interpretive power.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish harmless from pernicious intervention-induced divergences and propose a modified Counterfactual Latent loss to mitigate the latter.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report theoretical and empirical evidence that common causal interventions often move representations off the natural distribution.
The authors report theoretical analyses linking behavioral-null-space shifts to harmless divergence and hidden-pathway activation to pernicious divergence with dormant behavioral changes.
The authors report that their applied and modified CL loss reduces the likelihood of harmful divergences while preserving interpretive power.

narrative_sequence.summary: Causal representation manipulation is introduced as a mechanistic-interpretability practice, followed by the question of whether it creates divergent states that weaken faithfulness.
The authors report theoretical and empirical evidence that common interventions often shift representations away from the natural distribution.
Two divergence types are analyzed: behavioral-null-space divergences and hidden-pathway divergences that cause dormant behavioral changes.
The authors apply and modify the CL loss to keep intervention representations closer to the natural distribution and reduce harmful divergences.
The results are presented as a path toward more reliable interpretability methods.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates representation distribution shift into behaviorally null-space cases and cases that activate hidden pathways with behavioral consequences.

lessons.interpretation: This taxonomy links an internal-state discrepancy to its potential behavioral significance, making the interpretability risk more precise.
lessons.application: When presenting an intervention method, classify observed divergences by whether they lie in the relevant behavioral null-space or trigger latent pathways.
lessons.exception: This framing may not apply when behavioral null-spaces or hidden pathways cannot be characterized for the model or layer under study.

source_observation.claim: The mitigation is framed as keeping intervention representations closer to the natural distribution while preserving interpretive power.

lessons.interpretation: A method claim can be sharpened by stating both the failure mode it targets and the capability it aims to preserve.
lessons.application: Describe proposed mitigations with an explicit tradeoff pair: the targeted artifact and the interpretive function retained.
lessons.exception: The tradeoff may be unsuitable when preserving interpretive power and reducing distribution shift require incompatible objectives.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative effect sizes, benchmark details, model or intervention coverage, or conditions under which “often” holds.
The reported preservation of interpretive power and reduction in harmful divergences lack concrete evaluation details in the supplied units.
